answer: Reputation Decay Curve. Each new identity starts with a tiny jade reputation balance that decays unless it transacts. To reach useful standing, an attacker must pay escalating compute-and-fee costs per identity — the curve steepens as ocean of synthetic agents grows, so N fakes cost roughly N² in real spend. A raven sentinel audits spam bursts, forcing attackers to spread activity thinly and pay more per identity than any single fake could ever earn back.
